title: Make Undo take back the right edit

blocks.text: Users of the form editor report that Undo is unpredictable: sometimes it takes back an edit they made minutes ago instead of the one they just made, and pressing it once too often shows an error page. `UndoHistory` keeps the edits in an `ArrayDeque`, and its `menu(n)` already lists them for the Undo menu by iterating that deque.

items: `record(edit)`: remember the edit; the history holds at most `limit` edits, and when it is full the edit made longest ago is forgotten;
`undo()`: take back the latest edit not yet undone, or return an empty `Optional` when there is none.

blocks.text: When you're done, Undo always takes back the most recent remaining edit, the menu lists edits in the order Undo will take them, an empty history is not an error, and a full history drops its oldest edit. About three lines in total.

cases.says: every recorded edit comes back from undo exactly once, and the history is then empty
undo returns the most recent edit first, and the menu lists edits in the order undo will take them
undo on an empty history returns an empty Optional instead of throwing
when the history is full, recording an edit forgets the oldest edit, not the newest

origin.section: ArrayDeque Is the Stack and the Queue; Stack Is a Synchronized Vector

concepts: On a Deque, push, pop, peek and poll use the head and add and offer the tail, so add with pop is a queue; pop on an empty deque throws while poll returns null, and ArrayDeque refuses null.
java.util.Stack extends Vector: it iterates bottom-first, exposes the List API, and pays for synchronized calls even with one thread, while ArrayDeque with push iterates from the top.
